newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Neuhaus to tempt investors with March IPO.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Neuhaus to tempt investors with March IPO.

text.p: Sweet-toothed investors are to be tempted with a pre-Easter initial public offering of shares in chocolate maker Neuhaus, a household name in Belgium.

Brokerage Petercam, which is lead-managing the issue, said on Tuesday the shares are being issued by Dutch holding company Artal Nederland BV, which is controlled by Belgium's Wittouck and Ullens families.
The Brussels Stock Exchange said in a statement published in Belgian newspapers on Tuesday that it had received an application from Artal to list up to 750,000 shares in Neuhaus.

"Controlling shareholder Artal will be selling 60 percent of (the 750,000 shares) on the bourse at the moment of the initial public offering. It may be a little bit higher if there is a particularly strong demand from the market, but the main target is 60 percent," Petercam corporate finance director Pierre Lebeau told Reuters.
Lebeau said Petercam hoped the issue prospectus would be approved by Belgium's Banking and Finance Commission by mid-February and the listing take place in early March.

"We will not issue any indications of the pricing before marketing (of the IPO) starts in February," he said. "All I can tell you is that the pricing will reflect the fact Neuhaus is a growth company and offers also an interesting (dividend) yield for shareholders."
Neuhaus's financial year ends on June 30, but the company already had a good idea of its performance in the 1996/1997 period, Lebeau said.
"This is due to the fact the biggest part of sales are realised during the last quarter of the year in the run-up to Christmas," he said, declining to give details.
Belgian Trends magazine said on January 9 that the company expected 1996/1997 sales growing to 1.55 billion Belgian francs ($46.27 million) from 1.36 billion francs in 1995/1996.
Founded in 1857 by Swiss citizen Jean Neuhans, the chocolate house remained in the same family until 1978.

At present called Neuhaus-Mondose, the company has units in the U.K., the Netherlands, France, the U.S. and Japan. Its subsidiaries include French chocolate maker Jeff de Bruges and Martial, which in turn owns Britain's Thornton.
Lebeau said the company was at present in the process of changing its statutes so that it would be listed under the name of Neuhaus only.
